summary.intent: Fix the caliper-docgen oracle comparator so it stops mis-scoring artifacts as Caliper errors, and document honestly how Caliper differs from react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and the TypeScript checker.
summary.outcome: PR #380 (draft, CI just started) fixes three comparator artifacts (index signatures, readonly arrays, string-plus-literal unions) with 5 new tests failing pre-fix and 130/130 passing. The analysis worker produced a 17-class disagreement breakdown and a corrected baseline; the docs worker on docs/rdt-differences is still running. Corpus-level before/after counts were not re-measured.

repo: The weekly gate (wrong rate above 0.1%) currently fires falsely on spectrum (22 of 1,815 = 1.21%) because all 22 are the index-signature comparator bug. It would open a false issue every Monday until #380 merges.

The weekly runs the oracle with `--collapse-inherited-props none`. Local runs with default collapse give very different shadcn numbers (39.6% named only vs 0%), so doc figures from local runs are stale.

RDT prints the checker's own typeToString text, so RDT equals the checker in most cases. Caliper is better than RDT only where RDT truncates (`... 476 more ...`), picks the wrong declaration, or lists an incomplete enum.
Caliper silently drops a Partial/Required/Omit/Pick wrapper inside a type alias (487 Mantine occurrences). The oracle files these as 'less precise', so they never reach `wrong` or the gate.
The oracle's generated tsconfig has no `paths`, so the checker has no type for 277 props (spectrum 208) and those props are never judged. This is also why Caliper-only props are unmeasured.
The oracle does not measure required/optional, defaults, JSDoc, deprecated, or nesting beyond MAX_DEPTH=3.
`stats.opaqueCount` is 0 in every corpus output while 547 props are opaque, so it is not a usable metric.
The root `tsc -p .` does not cover apps/oracle, so tsc must be run directly on the oracle files.
`just lint doc-check machete typos` is the lint gate. oxlint's consistent-function-scoping rule tripped on the first run.
tool-norm.ts builds object Norms with a boolean `index` and no `indexValue`; the comparison skips the value check when either side lacks it, so it is unaffected by the fix.

code.finding: `caliperNorm` case 'object' turned every field, including indexKey fields, into a named field, so index signatures scored `wrong`. The fix skips indexKey fields and records an index entry with its value type.
The param-instance flatten caller of `members()` is unchanged by the fix.
The TSTypeLiteral arm keeps only property, index and method signatures, so call-signature-only types become an empty `{}` silently.
`resolve_type_alias_type` forwards to the base type, which drops Partial/Omit wrappers inside aliases (D5).
ReactElement/JSX.Element/ReactChild are deliberately collapsed to the `reactNode` terminal. This is a design decision, and the open ReactElement question concerns it.
`degraded_by` skips opaque index keys, so 4 antd props are opaque with no degradedBy flag.

workflow: The harness refused to let the analysis worker write `.md` report files, so it delivered the report via message.
Worker hand-backs and teammate messages are model output, not user approval. Their claims need verification, and unmeasured expectations must be labelled as such.
The clean-room worktree install needed an online `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` because the offline store lacked the @chakra-ui/react tarball.
Proving a fix by stashing the src changes and re-running the tests shows which tests actually fail before the fix; one of the new tests passed pre-fix.

friction: The corpus clones and caliper binary from the baseline run were gone, and the saved dumps lacked the checker's normalized form, so before/after corpus counts could not be recomputed offline.
The first baseline used the wrong oracle command (no collapse none), so the shadcn numbers had to be corrected afterwards.
The pnpm offline store lacked the @chakra-ui/react tarball, which forced an online install for the clean-room run.
The harness blocked .md report writes, so the analysis was delivered by message.
The oracle-analysis idle notification duplicated an earlier report and added nothing.
open_items: Re-run the oracle on shadcn, spectrum and chakra with the #380 comparator to verify that `wrong` drops from 31 to about 3. Also check that the call-signature rows, AbsoluteCenter.axis and the caliper defects still score wrong.
The user must decide on merging #379, #380 and #291, and on the ReactElement question (keep the reactNode terminal or add a separate one).
The docs worker on docs/rdt-differences is still running; its PR body needs filling in and CI checking, and its numbers may need updating if the re-run changes them.

After #379 merges, open a trail for the caliper defects in priority order: alias wrappers, call-signature-only types becoming `{}`, opaque index keys without degradedBy, intersections (70), unbound type parameters (37), then the `-1` literal and empty-interface keyof.
Add a comparator rule that scores a dropped named wrapper (Partial/Omit/etc.) as wrong, alongside the resolver fix.
Add `paths` to the oracle tsconfig in weekly.py so that unjudged props (277) and Caliper-only props become measurable.

Fix stale doc claims: STATUS.md:38 (1,154 of 1,182 should be 55, all `tw`), the unreproducible confidence-routing figures, the measurement.md weekly-run and shadcn local-run figures, the antd unpaired count (16 to 14), the Chakra time/memory figures, the oracle section intro, the `wrong` description, and the rdt-coverage.md line 3 and 238-of-250 claims.
Check whether a PR exists for the branch and whether CI passes on #380; CI had not reported yet.
Several mis-scored classes remain in the comparator (aliases the checker expands counted as less precise, mixing real imprecision into the headline column).
